subject: Performance SLO: context window / max tokens impact on latency — follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@finco.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO: context window / max tokens impact on latency — post-call recap

Thanks again for your time this morning, James and Priya — good call. Quick recap of the product/infra items we covered and the next steps to get you a concrete SLO proposal: 

- Context window: you mentioned inputs up to ~40k tokens for batch analysis, and typical conversational inputs in prod will be closer to 4–8k tokens. Outputs range 512–2k tokens depending on the flow.
- Target latency: interactive agents require <= 500ms tail p95 for short convo turns (<=1k input tokens). For the long-batch analyses we discussed, throughput/throughput latency trade-offs are acceptable (batch jobs can be ~2–10s).
- Concurrency & throughput: initial rollout expected ~100 QPS for embeddings/rerank requests, peak concurrency for generation routes ~40 concurrent streams.
- Streaming: you flagged a preference for partial output streaming for agent responses to reduce perceived latency for long outputs.

Attachments: I attached our SLO template and a short matrix showing how input+output token counts map to expected latency on our dedicated configs. Also included samples you promised to share (request logs) — that will help us size concurrency and batching.

Next steps:
1) We will validate expected p95/p99 latency for the 1k/4k/40k input buckets and get a sizing recommendation (Vivek + infra) — ETA Wed EOD (tomorrow).
2) You’ll share a small redacted sample of representative requests and a recent traffic profile (Priya).
3) We’ll draft a proposed SLO table and call out recommended routing/fallback policies for the first 90-day rollout.

Let me know if I missed anything.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_slo_template.pdf (7 pages)
Attachment: context-window-latency-matrix.xlsx (1 sheet)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: James Li <james.li@finco.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: context window / max tokens impact on latency — sizing notes

Marissa — notes from infra side after reviewing call recording and the preliminary numbers James shared: 

- Short conv (<=1k tokens in+out): achievable p95 ~250–400ms on our Dedicated M-profile (2x A100-equivalent) with single-request KV cache warm and minimal batching. p99 may hit ~520ms depending on model headroom.
- Mid conv (4–8k tokens): p95 moves to ~700–900ms if we execute without KV prefix caching; with aggressive prefix caching (your conversational patterns), p95 drops to ~400–600ms.
- Large context batch (20–40k tokens): best-effort latency is in the 2–8s range. We recommend treating these as asynchronous batch jobs rather than synchronous user-facing streams.
- Streaming: enabling partial streaming reduces perceived latency but increases compute and memory pressure; recommended to enable streaming for conversational routes with outputs >512 tokens and to limit streaming window size to 512 token chunks.
- Concurrency: given 40 concurrent streams and our batching logic, expect ~10–20% throughput reduction versus fully batched offline jobs. If FinCo wants deterministic p95 SLAs at high concurrency, we recommend reserving dedicated pool capacity (Dedicated) with headroom for peaks.

Open question for pricing/sla: what p99 target does FinCo need for interactive flows? If they require <800ms p99, we’ll need a higher guaranteed capacity tier.

I’ll run a quick set of synthetic runs tomorrow morning using the sample prompt distributions and attach latency histograms.

—Vivek
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: infra-latency-initial-estimates.png (histogram)
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: James Li <james.li@finco.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: context window / max tokens impact on latency — follow-up

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- For the interactive agent route we are aiming for a p95 <= 500ms and p99 <= 1.2s for typical convs (~500–1k tokens). We can accept higher latencies for the scheduled batch analytics jobs.
- For streaming we want progressive tokens to appear within 200–300ms for the first chunk if possible (helps UX on agent handoffs).
- We’ll share a redacted traffic extract (Priya) and a sample of the longest/context-heavy prompts (James) by EOD today.

Would appreciate Vivek’s histograms once available.

—Priya
Head of Product Engineering, FinCo Capital
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@finco.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: context window / max tokens impact on latency — next steps

James / Priya — thanks for the clarifications and for committing to share the logs. Quick plan/timeline based on Vivek’s runs: 

- Tomorrow EOD (Wed): Vivek will upload the synthetic latency histograms and an initial recommended SLO table for the 3 buckets (<=1k, 4–8k, 20–40k).
- Thu: We’ll ingest your redacted logs and run an empirical sizing pass. Expect a sizing/price estimate Fri by EOD.
- For interactive p95 <=500ms and p99 <=1.2s target: initial recommendation is Dedicated M-profile with 20% headroom and streaming enabled for >512 token outputs. We’ll call out exact concurrency limits and fallback policies in the SLO doc.

Action items for FinCo:
- Priya/Jame s: share redacted logs + representative prompts (EOD today).
- Confirm whether 512-token streaming chunk size is acceptable or you prefer 256.

I’ll send the draft SLO table + DocuSign for the pilot commitment once we have the sizing.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
